name: HBM supply (SK Hynix / Micron / Samsung)
description_md: High-bandwidth memory is the co-packaged DRAM every AI accelerator needs — 8+ stacks per Rubin-class GPU — and only three companies make it. SK Hynix leads with ~60% of the HBM market (58-62% in Q1-26 depending on tracker) and is reported to supply about two-thirds of Nvidia's HBM4 for the Vera Rubin platform; Micron told investors its HBM capacity is sold out through 2026 (~$8B annualized HBM run-rate); Samsung, after trailing on HBM3E qualification, is ramping HBM4 and targeting early delivery to claw back share. Demand exceeds supply so structurally that customers now pay in advance: Nvidia reportedly prepaid SK Hynix and Micron $540-770M each to lock allocation, and paid HBM4 samples shipped ahead of Q1-26 contract finalization. HBM also consumes ~3x the wafer area of standard DRAM per bit, so its growth cannibalizes conventional DRAM supply — spreading the shortage across the whole memory market (the 2026 pricing super-cycle). Status basis: judged binding — all three suppliers effectively sold out through 2026, prepayments as rationing mechanism, and packaging-integrated qualification makes switching slow.

dependents.dependency_md: Largest HBM buyer worldwide; Rubin-generation HBM4 demand allocated ~2/3 SK Hynix. Reportedly prepaid $540-770M each to SK Hynix and Micron to secure 2026-27 supply — memory, with packaging, sets the unit ceiling.
MI400-series bandwidth advantage depends on HBM4 allocation from the same three suppliers, where AMD is the smaller customer.
Every custom XPU (TPU et al.) ships with HBM; hyperscaler ASIC programs compete for the residual allocation after Nvidia.

substitutes_md: No drop-in substitute: accelerator memory bandwidth requirements can only be met by HBM today. Partial relief valves — LPDDR/GDDR for inference-optimized parts, larger SRAM caches (Cerebras-style), or CXL-attached DRAM — serve niches, not frontier training. Switching between the three HBM vendors requires months of electrical/thermal qualification against a specific GPU and its CoWoS package, which is why allocation is contracted a year ahead. Samsung's HBM4 ramp is the main share-shift mechanism, not a fourth source; Chinese HBM (CXMT) remains generations behind and export-restricted.
downcycle_md: Memory is the most cyclical layer of the chain, and HBM would not be exempt: the same fabs flex between HBM and commodity DRAM, so an AI demand fall converts today's shortage into a general DRAM glut (as capacity built for HBM floods back into conventional bits). Prepayments and 2026 long-term agreements protect near-term revenue — Nvidia's advances are effectively non-refundable capacity reservations — but 2027+ volumes are re-negotiable, and history (2019, 2023) shows memory pricing can halve within a year. Samsung, the latest entrant with the most speculative HBM4 capacity, would absorb the swing first; SK Hynix's concentration (majority of profit from one customer's flagship platform) turns from moat to risk. Watch: paid-sample terms, prepayment size, and the HBM/DRAM price spread as contract-quality indicators.
